images.filename: Staying close to the mother in all situations.jpg
images.caption: Dusky Langurs live and feed on the upper part of the forest canopy. They transit from one tree to another by jumping, often in a spectacular and daring manner. From birth the infant will cling to the mothers belly during these daring leaps.
images.alt: Dusky Langurs live and feed on the upper part of the forest canopy. They transit from one tree to another by jumping, often in a spectacular and daring manner. From birth the infant will cling to the mothers belly during these daring leaps.

images.filename: Dusky Langur infant holding on while its mother leaps.jpg
images.caption: It is amazing how strong the grip on the Dusky Langur infant must be. From day one it grips its mother's fur while she goes about her normal life feeding in the forest canopy. In leaping the mother will have one arm around the infant to start but uses both of her arms outstretched for landing. The life of the infant depends on its grip.
images.alt: It is amazing how strong the grip on the Dusky Langur infant must be. From day one it grips its mother's fur while she goes about her normal life feeding in the forest canopy. In leaping the mother will have one arm around the infant to start but uses both of her arms outstretched for landing. The life of the infant depends on its grip.

images.filename: Dusky Langur infant learning to eat leaves.jpg
images.caption: The Dusky Langur infant is breast-fed every 90 minutes in the first few months of its life. It watches it mother eating leaves, flowers and fruit and in this photo the infant seems bemused in a lesson on eating leaves.
images.alt: The Dusky Langur infant is breast-fed every 90 minutes in the first few months of its life. It watches it mother eating leaves, flowers and fruit and in this photo the infant seems bemused in a lesson on eating leaves.

images.filename: The orange coloured infant Dusky Langur starts to turn black.jpg
images.caption: Around three to four months of age the infant Dusky Langur becomes more autonomous and starts to take on the colour of the adults. The fur turns progressively grey and the feet and hands turn black. At this stage the mother appears to get less assistance from the other members of the troop.
images.alt: Around three to four months of age the infant Dusky Langur becomes more autonomous and starts to take on the colour of the adults. The fur turns progressively grey and the feet and hands turn black. At this stage the mother appears to get less assistance from the other members of the troop.
